findings: src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp BitpackingSelect: a general `select` callback for the default integer compression. It does not check for any particular query, table or data. It only runs through StandardColumnData::Select, and only when the whole vector is scanned, sits in one segment, and the validity column also has select. Updates, segment boundaries and force_fetch_row all keep the old path.

Each mode matches BitpackingScanPartial. CONSTANT and CONSTANT_DELTA use the same multiplier, group_offset + i, with unsigned wrapping. FOR adds the frame of reference as T_U, which gives the same result as ApplyFrameOfReference. The uhugeint→hugeint casts are plain bit casts, so they cannot throw. DELTA_FOR decodes every block in order and carries current_delta_offset forward, as Skip and ScanPartial do. current_group_offset and LoadNextGroup advance exactly as in ScanPartial.

Direct bit extraction is correct for the LSB-first fastpforlib layout: block_offset is a multiple of 32, so the block start falls on a byte, and the memcpy reads at most ceil((shift+width)/8) ≤ 8 bytes, never past the end of the block. Width 0 gives a 0-byte memcpy and a mask of 0, which is fine. Width > 56, and 1-, 2- and 16-byte types, fall back to unpacking only the blocks that hold a selected row.
Dense path (more than 25% of rows pass): full ScanPartial, then compaction in place. This is safe because sel is ascending (source_idx >= i). The result is FLAT, as the select contract requires.

src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp: the new exact-bitmap tier is capped at 2^27 bits (16MB) and the count*1024 product cannot overflow. It is a general sizing heuristic, and the existing 2^32 guard is unchanged.
The issue says the warm JSON profile was not collected, and the contribution of each part was not measured separately. That does not affect correctness.
